slot.brief: A boat crossing a river with given still-water speed and river speed; find heading to reach the opposite point and the time of crossing by solving velocity-vector components.

stem: A boat moves at $5$ m s$^{-1}$ in still water while a river flows at $3$ m s$^{-1}$. To reach the point directly opposite across a $120$ m wide river, find its heading upstream from the perpendicular to the bank and its crossing time.

verdicts.working: Cancel the river current: 5 sin θ = 3, so θ = 36.9° upstream. Across-river speed = 5 cos θ = 4 m/s, giving time = 120/4 = 30 s.

working:
$5\sin\theta=3\Rightarrow\theta=36.9^\circ$; across-river speed $=5\cos\theta=4$ m s$^{-1}$.\\
$t=120/4=30$ s.

Independent check: Cancel the river current: 5 sin θ = 3, so θ = 36.9° upstream. Across-river speed = 5 cos θ = 4 m/s, giving time = 120/4 = 30 s.
solution: For the boat to land directly opposite, its upstream velocity component must cancel the river flow: $5\sin\theta=3$, so $\theta=36.9^\circ$. The across-river speed is $5\cos\theta=4\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, hence $$t=\frac{120}{4}=30\,\text{s}.$$
